t: The Swiss, about 22,000 strong and almost all pikemen, charged the French guns twice, on the evening of 13 September and the morning of 14 September, and were held by massed cannon fire and cavalry charges.
The battle hung in the balance until the Venetian forces under Bartolomeo d'Alviano arrived in the mid-morning, after which the Swiss withdrew in a single large open square.
The Treaty of Fribourg of 1516, the Perpetual Peace, lasted until the French Revolutionary Wars and opened three centuries of close ties between the Swiss Confederacy and France.
dyk: Francis I had a medal struck with the words 'I have vanquished those whom only Caesar vanquished', and asked to be knighted on the battlefield by the Chevalier Bayard.
ev: The Swiss win at Novara, take control of Milan and restore Maximilian Sforza as duke
Francis I leads his army over the Col d'Argentière, and the French capture the papal commander Prospero Colonna at Villafranca
Swiss columns of about 22,000 leave Milan and meet the French at Marignano, where the fighting lasts into the night
The Swiss attack again in the morning, and the arrival of the Venetians turns the battle against them
Francis meets Pope Leo X at Bologna, and the two agree the terms of a concordat
The Treaty of Fribourg, the Perpetual Peace, is signed between Francis and the Swiss cantons
France and the Swiss Confederacy conclude a service pact that makes Swiss regiments a regular part of the French armed forces

f.place: Near the town now called Melegnano, 16 km south-east of Milan, in Lombardy, Italy, on a plain of vineyards, fields, orchards and pastures near San Giuliano
f.sides: France under Francis I, with German landsknechts and Venetian allies under Bartolomeo d'Alviano who arrived in the morning of the second day; the Swiss, about 22,000 men, almost all pike infantry with fewer than a dozen guns. The Swiss were heavily outnumbered and outgunned.
f.outcome: A French victory: the Swiss withdrew in good order, the French regained Milan, and the Treaty of Fribourg of 1516 ended Swiss claims to the protectorate of Milan.
